newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - March 28.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - March 28.

text.p: Random Lengths Gross List Cash Lumber Prices Quotes:
(2x4 Std&Btr) WEEKLY MIDWEEK PREV WK YR AGO
COMMENT - A distributor-led pickup on Wednesday erased a slow early-week start and put lumber prices on firmer footing, according to the Random Lengths weekly lumber market report.
The faster pace was sparked by better weather that boosted consumption and improved buyers' cash flow.

While sales were by no means a runaway, the flurry cleaned up producers' prompt loadings and took some of the heat off of some bloated reload stocks. Wholesalers bought a little more wood, but stayed cuatious. Many retailers remained skeptical, steadfastly holding to the "wall of wood" theory. Treaters reported a pickup in sales, but were slow to replace at current prices. An interest rate increase announced Tuesday had already been fctored into trading and consequently had little impact. In the wake of the Fed's announcement, traders split over whether higher rates would initially slow housing sales or might pull in some undecided buyers.

Prices were slow to recover from early softness as some mills focused on fattening order files and kept a light foot on the price accelerator. A few end-of-the-month bargains surfaced, mostly early in the week, and generally got snapped up on counters from mills' asking levels.
The emphasis tilted away from truckload volumes of highly specified tallies and toward carloads.

However, some producers in the West reported they were still struggling with tight car supplies that slowed rail shipments. Better weather brought improving log supplies in the South, though some Southern Pine mills continued to run hand-to-mouth.

Meanwhile, road bans slowed jobsite activity in the Upper Midwest. Sales of boards lacked spark, except in Southern Pine, where strength was unabated. Prices of Ponderosa Pine industrials were firm to up.
